Subject: Recap + procurement velocity options (PO vs card vs marketplace)

Hi Samir / Jessa — thanks again for a quick, focused demo earlier. A concise recap and three suggested paths to speed procurement so Brightwell can get live with Redwood in March:

Summary of what you said you need:
- Sandbox access for privacy testing (2–4 engineers)
- SOC2 artifacts + network diagram for internal security review
- A commercial route that avoids month-long PO cycles if possible

Three commercial paths (tradeoffs):
1) Card trial + monthly card payments: fastest to start (hours), limited for scale, easiest for PLG testing.
2) PO with standard terms: typical enterprise path, requires legal review and finance sign-off (3–6 weeks typical).
3) Cloud marketplace listing (AWS/Azure/GCP): longer onboarding but maps to procurement for many enterprise buyers and simplifies internal billing (4–8 weeks).

Immediate asks / next steps I think will move this forward:
- Samir: confirm whether Procurement will accept marketplace invoices or needs a PO. If you prefer PO, send a point of contact and preferred PO template.
- Jessa: can your security team review the sandbox on our transient VPC? I attached the test checklist you mentioned.
- Marissa / Karthik: internally we should prepare a DPA + SOC2 package and a short MAP (mutual action plan) to reflect whichever path they pick.

I attached Brightwell-Questions-20270201.pdf (your checklist annotated) and a one-page MAP draft. If card is acceptable we can enable a small $10k card spend within 24 hours. If PO is required, I propose the following timeline and milestones below (legal -> security -> finance -> PO issuance).

Proposed PO path timeline (if chosen):
- Day 0: NA demo + kickoff (done)
- Day 1–3: Redwood sends draft DPA + SOW + SOC2 package (we will)
- Day 4–10: Brightwell legal/security review
- Day 11–18: Finance approvals and PO template alignment
- Day 19–28: PO issuance and account activation

I can lead coordination and set weekly 20-minute touchpoints. If you prefer we can also try a hybrid: start sandbox on card while parallelizing PO review.

Thanks — notes below and I’ll follow up with a short MAP spreadsheet for sign-off.

Best,

Thanks Naomi — useful recap. A few clarifying datapoints from our side:
- Procurement prefers a PO for anything > $5k/month, but will accept marketplace charges under specific vendor policy if vendor is listed.
- Security needs the network diagram + a 3-day sandbox window. They don’t signoff on vendor-managed keys without legal approval.
- Finance will need a signed DPA and a SOW with pricing line items to process a PO.

We’re inclined to go PO for production, but we can do an initial sandbox on a corporate card to shorten the evaluation. Procurement: I’ve looped you in — can you share the PO template (ours) and turnaround time?
